Consult Summary:
- Adult patient presented via teleconsult with 2-day history of constant, worsening lower abdominal pain (below umbilicus) with mild nausea, subjective fever/sweats, urinary frequency, and pink urine; empirically treated for possible UTI with trimethoprim; advised pregnancy testing, hydration, analgesia, and close follow-up with safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal pain, just below the belly button; sore to press; described as burning; localized without radiation.
- Onset/duration: Started ~2 days ago.
- Course: Gradually worsening; constant; patient remains able to function.
- Bowel symptoms: Constipation last week (now resolved); no diarrhea; bowel movements currently normal.
- Urinary symptoms: Increased frequency; urine noticed to be “pink” at times; no dysuria (no burning/stinging). Uncertain if true hematuria.
- Nausea/vomiting: Mild nausea; no vomiting.
- Fever: Feels hot and sweaty; no temperature measured.
- Sexual/gynecologic history: Sexually active with same partner; last intercourse ~4 days ago. Contraception: Implanon inserted ~1 year ago. Last STI screen ~6 months ago, reported normal. Last menstrual period reported as “about three weeks ago” then “two weeks ago” (conflict noted). Patient considers pregnancy unlikely but possible; advised to test.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives): No shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headaches, or vision problems.

Past Medical History:
- Generally well; no prior similar episodes.
- Surgical history: Denies any prior surgeries.
- Other chronic conditions: Not mentioned.

Medications:
- Implanon (contraceptive implant) inserted ~1 year ago; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- New prescription: Trimethoprim “1 tablet twice daily for 3 days”; dose (mg) and route not documented.
- Analgesia advice: Paracetamol recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Living situation: Share house with two roommates.
- Occupation: Accountant.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks socially; not more than usual per patient.
- Substance use: Not documented.

Family History:
- Denies family history related to bowel disease; otherwise not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals documented.
- No physical exam findings documented.

Investigations:
- None completed at this visit.
- Pregnancy test recommended (not yet done).
- Clinician initially proposed tests to evaluate cause; patient opted for empiric antibiotics first.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Lower abdominal pain with urinary frequency and pink urine; possible urinary tract infection (UTI) versus gastrointestinal or pregnancy-related cause.
  - Plan:
    - Start empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose in mg and route not documented).
    - Hydration encouraged; consider cranberry juice.
    - Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Perform pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy.
    - Safety-net: Return if symptoms not improving in a few days or if worsening abdominal pain, persistent feeling hot/sweaty or measured fever, or vomiting.
- Issue 2: Pink urine (possible hematuria) without dysuria.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor urine color; if persistent or worsening, follow up for urinalysis/urine culture and further evaluation.
- Issue 3: Contraception/pregnancy risk.
  - Plan:
    - Verify negative pregnancy test; continue current contraception. No changes made today.
- General:
  - Prescription sent electronically to pharmacy; start today.
  - Call the clinic if any new concerns arise.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Drug allergies not documented.
  - Vital signs not recorded.
  - Physical examination not documented.
  - No objective temperature measurement.
  - No urinalysis/urine culture performed at this visit.
  - Pregnancy test not yet performed.
  - Medication doses/routes/frequencies largely not documented (except frequency/duration for trimethoprim).
- Internal conflicts:
  - Last menstrual period stated as “about three weeks ago” then “two weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Patient name referenced as “Tim” and later “Kim” (conflict noted).
  - Hematuria uncertain: patient reported “pink” urine but unsure if blood present.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor filler words and brief hesitations but clinically interpretable.
